# `intent st`

**Generated by `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/gen_reference.sh` at 2026-09-24 20:57Z. Do not edit -- re-run it.**

Manage steel threads for the project

|                                      |                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Revision this describes              | `e2f5ce4b3201417247fcca9ebc17848f967d0e38` (`HEAD`) |
| Release presence is reported against | `v3.2.0`                                            |

**The register is a declaration, not a behaviour claim.** The command surface is built from `surface/dispatch-table.json`, so the register at a revision states what that revision exposes. It does not state that any of it works. Where this page and your binary disagree, **your binary is right**.

**No exit codes are listed per command.** The register's per-command exit tables are measurements of _v2_, and v3 does not reproduce them everywhere, so they are not published here as v3's contract. Every command follows the one surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes).

## The commands

| Command               | What it does                                                                                                                                           | In v3.2.0 | Reads or writes | Undo       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| `intent st`           | Manage steel threads for the project                                                                                                                   | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent st new`       | Create a new steel thread                                                                                                                              | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st start`     | Mark a steel thread as in progress                                                                                                                     | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st done`      | Mark a steel thread as complete                                                                                                                        | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st cancel`    | Mark a steel thread as cancelled, with a reason                                                                                                        | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st triage`    | Move a triaged thread out of Triage into NotStarted                                                                                                    | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st hold`      | Put a thread on hold, with a reason                                                                                                                    | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st resume`    | Take a thread off hold and back into Wip                                                                                                               | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st reopen`    | Reopen a completed thread back into Wip, with a reason                                                                                                 | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st reinstate` | Reinstate a cancelled thread into NotStarted, with a reason                                                                                            | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st hydrate`   | Add a steel thread to .intentfiles and write its files                                                                                                 | yes       | mutate          | idempotent |
| `intent st dehydrate` | Remove a steel thread from .intentfiles and delete its files                                                                                           | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st list`      | List steel threads (default: in progress only)                                                                                                         | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent st show`      | Show details of a specific steel thread                                                                                                                | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent st edit`      | Open a steel thread file, realising the thread if it is not on disk: in $VISUAL or $EDITOR on a terminal, and as a printed path when stdout is not one | yes       | mutate          | idempotent |
| `intent st attach`    | Write an attachment's content from a local file                                                                                                        | yes       | mutate          | one-way    |
| `intent st detach`    | Remove an attachment from a thread, leaving its file on disk for you to delete                                                                         | yes       | mutate          | one-way    |
| `intent st renumber`  | Move a steel thread to a free id, with everything that names it structurally                                                                           | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st relate`    | Link a thread to another, or replace the note on a link it already carries                                                                             | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st unrelate`  | Drop a thread's link to another, including a link to a thread that no longer exists                                                                    | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent st sync`      | Print the steel thread index; with `--write`, write it and each thread's projection to disk                                                            | yes       | mutate          | idempotent |

## Retired

These do not exist in v3. They refuse with an exit code that distinguishes _removed_ from _never built_, so a v2-era script gets an answer rather than an unknown-command error.

| Command               | What it did in v2                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `intent st repair`    | Repair malformed steel thread metadata                                                                                             |
| `intent st organize`  | Organize ST files in directories by status                                                                                         |
| `intent st bootstrap` | Retrofit ST0000 deliverables into a brownfield project -- audit what is present, missing or partial, then install the missing ones |

## `intent st`

Manage steel threads for the project

```
intent st <command>
```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.2.0`     | yes                                                        |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | no                                                         |

**Arguments**

| Argument  | Type         | Required | Values | Notes |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `command` | `subcommand` | yes      |        |       |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent st --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent st new`

Create a new steel thread

```
intent st new <title> [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.2.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | reversible |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type     | Required | Values | Notes                                                                                                  |
| -------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`  | `string` | yes      |        | Exactly one title; quote it if it has spaces. A second positional is refused as a usage error, exit 1. |

**Flags**

| Flag            | Takes | Default | What it does                                |
| --------------- | ----- | ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `-s`, `--start` | no    |         | Mark the new thread in progress immediately |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent st new --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent st done`

## `intent st list`


**Flags**

| Flag         | Takes            | Default    | What it does                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |

## `intent st edit`

Open a steel thread file, realising the thread if it is not on disk: in $VISUAL or $EDITOR on a terminal, and as a printed path when stdout is not one

```
intent st edit <id> [<file>] [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.2.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | idempotent |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type    | Required | Values                                          | Notes                                                                          |
| -------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`     | `st-id` | yes      |                                                 |                                                                                |
| `file`   | `enum`  | no       | `info`, `design`, `impl`, `tasks`, `acceptance` | Which file. Unlike `st show`, `all` is refused, because it has no single path. |

**Flags**

| Flag       | Takes | Default | What it does                                            |
| ---------- | ----- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--editor` | no    |         | Open the file in $VISUAL or $EDITOR, whatever stdout is |
| `--path`   | no    |         | Print the path and open nothing, whatever stdout is     |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent st edit --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## Refusals

**There is no per-command refusal list, because the register does not carry one.** A row declares its path, arguments, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, MCP exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it refuses.

The estate-wide roster of refusal variants is in [what Intent ships at this revision](cut-surface.md), taken from a roster that declares itself exhaustive and is checked as one. **It is not attributed to commands anywhere**, and attributing it by reading the variant names would be a guess dressed as a reference.
